thread:
Maya (runtime): Quick heads-up — p99 token latency is spiking in us-west1 GPU pools since ~02:10 UTC, looks like continuous batching pressure + max_batch hitting hard.
Ryan (oncall): Noted. Any evidence it's an admission/backpressure issue vs networking?
Maya (runtime): Dashboard shows request queue growth on shard groups serving long-context models. GPU occupancy steady ~95%, but packer queues are piling up. Logs show repeated `Max batch reached, admitting=0` from admission-controller.
Praveen: Link to the dashboard?
Maya (runtime): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/ruckus/batching?orgId=1&var-region=us-west1 — p95 latency up 2.3x, p99 up 3.8x for the affected model tag `t5-long-v2`.
Julia: infra-bot just fired a saturation alert for us-west1-gpu-pool-7.
infra-bot: ALERT: pool us-west1-gpu-pool-7 saturation >= 90% for 12m. Recommending admission throttling.
Ryan (oncall): Can we confirm if `max_batch` env came back to 128 after last deploy? We rolled a packing improvement yesterday.
Maya (runtime): Yes — yesterday's deploy changed default `max_batch=128` for older quantized variants. That helped throughput on steady loads but seems to exacerbate tail during bursty arrivals (large variance in seq len). Continuous small arrivals cause large pack windows to form and KV cache churn.
Praveen: Seeing admission tokens exhaustion logs too: `admission_token_bucket: tokens=0 waiters=37`. That's the gate.
Maya (runtime): Example log snippet from shard-7:
```
[2026-03-18T02:12:03Z] gpu-queue shard=7 queue_len=142 max_batch=128 admitted=0 drop_policy=reject p99=468ms
[2026-03-18T02:12:07Z] admission-controller shard=7 tokens=0 waiters=52 reason=max-batch-pressure
```
Ryan (oncall): Oof. That explains the SLO misses. We need a fast mitigation path before next peak.
Julia: Suggestions? Reduce `max_batch`? Temporarily scale pool? Route some traffic to a cheaper, lower-latency instance?
Praveen: Quick options ranked: 1) Lower `max_batch` to 64 for `t5-long-v2` variant (low-risk config flip). 2) Increase admission token bucket refill rate (risk: cost spike if sustained). 3) Emergency vertical scale of one additional GPU node in pool (takes ~6-8m to come up).
Maya (runtime): I vote 1 + 3. Reduce batch size to drop packing headroom and reduce prefill/KV churn; also spin one warm pod to hit autoscaler fast-path.
Ryan (oncall): If we do (1), any downstream correctness or cost concerns?
Praveen: Lower max_batch reduces per-token throughput efficiency, cost/unit rises a bit, but latency tail should improve. For short-term it's acceptable.
Maya (runtime): I'll push a canary config change to admission controller for `t5-long-v2` in us-west1 only. Patch:
```
admission:
  model_overrides:
    t5-long-v2:
      max_batch: 64
      token_bucket_rate: 2500
```
We'll canary to shard-7 then roll to the pool if p99 improves.
Ryan (oncall): Go for canary. I'll start a node scale request now (k8s autoscaler override +1) so capacity is available if needed.
Julia: Notifying customer success? We might see transient increased cost, and a few in-flight requests may get rejected while admission config flips.
Maya (runtime): I'll add a fallback route in routing policy to redirect heavy requests to `t5-reduced-v1` (shorter context, quantized) if admission rejects. Simple flag flip in routing map.
SRE-Alerting: NOTE: incident created #INC-5209 "us-west1 batch admission pressure -> latency SLO miss". Escalation to eng-runtime and infra.
Praveen: After canary, capture these metrics: queue_len, admitted_per_sec, token_bucket_tokens, p99 latency, and KV cache miss rate. Also check headroom with packing acceptance rate.
Maya (runtime): Canary pushed to shard-7 at 02:18 UTC. Monitoring: p99 on shard-7 dropped from 470ms -> 220ms within 90s. Global p99 still elevated until canary expands.
Ryan (oncall): Autoscaler request responded: one warm node scheduled, ready 02:25 UTC.
Julia: Good. What's the rollback plan if something breaks?
Maya (runtime): Rollback is immediate revert to prior admission config via the cluster config manager (takes <30s) + remove routing fallback. We'll also tag any user-facing rejections for follow-up.
Praveen: Medium-term: we should add dynamic max_batch per-shard based on recent inter-arrival variance and KV cache pressure. Also consider admission token per-model (not just per-shard).
Maya (runtime): Agreed. Opening a follow-up RFC with simulation: dynamic max_batch, bucket autoscaling, and admission-aware autoscaler signals.
Ryan (oncall): For tonight, action items: Maya -> complete canary roll and monitor (30m), Ryan -> keep node + monitor cost alarms, Praveen -> prepare rollback patch, Julia -> message CS if anything customer-facing.
Maya (runtime): Will update thread with final state. :thumbsup:
(10m later) Maya (runtime): Canary complete — rolled out pool-wide at 02:29 UTC. p99 for affected model stabilized ~210-260ms. KV cache churn dropped ~40%.
Ryan (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Please follow up with postmortem and cost impact estimate.
Maya (runtime): Will author postmortem. Initial cost hit estimate: +6% on token compute for the next billing window if traffic stays this shape.
Praveen: Adding this to backlog: admission controller feature work and an e2e test that exercises high-variance arrival patterns.
Julia: Thanks team. Closing loop on CS once postmortem is ready. :white_check_mark:
